name: Parachute Ant
imitates: A low-riding ant on a small hook with a white post you can see; fished any time ants are around, especially late spring through fall.

steps.text: Wrap a thread base from the middle of the shank back to the bend.
Dub a thin layer on the thread and build an oblong ball from the bend to about the 40 percent point.
Bring the thread forward to the 80 percent point and tie in a length of Float-Viz with X wraps across its center, like spinner wings.
Pull both halves up into one post and post the base with thread wraps.
Strip the base of a grizzly hackle and tie it in just ahead of the post, shiny side down, then pull it up and wrap thread up the post to anchor it.
Return the thread to the base of the post and build a smaller dubbed ball behind the eye, leaving bare shank between the two balls as the waist.
Wrap the hackle down the post, each turn under the last, four or five turns. Pinch-wrap the tip down on the far side of the hook.
Whip finish behind the eye, trim the post to about one shank length and add a drop of head cement at the post base.
